Get Started.title: What to expect at your first visit

paragraphs.text: Your first visit begins with a complimentary consultation where the doctor examines your teeth, takes digital images and scans, and discusses your smile goals and treatment options. Expect a focused exam with digital photos/scans (such as iTero), an overview of choices including Damon Braces, Damon Clear, and clear aligners like Invisalign<sup>®</sup>, and a personalized treatment plan created for your needs.

We review medical and dental history, answer questions about risks and benefits, and discuss insurance and payment options. Bring your insurance card and any recent dental X‑rays if available; the team can verify coverage and recommend steps such as improving oral hygiene or a dental cleaning before treatment if needed.

image.alt: Father with daughter at reception of dentist's surgery

paragraphs.text: We offer interest-free payment plans and flexible monthly options to help make treatment manageable. Family discounts are available when multiple family members receive care.

The practice works with most insurance carriers and can help verify benefits and file claims to reduce out-of-pocket costs. Complimentary, no‑obligation consultations are available — schedule a free consult to begin.

image.alt: Enjoying time together

image.alt: Smiling patients receiving orthodontic care

paragraphs.text: A first orthodontic check around ages 7 to 9 helps us watch jaw growth and the way adult teeth come in. Early, targeted care can guide growth, create space for permanent teeth, and reduce the need for more complex treatment later.

We commonly treat crossbites, severe crowding or spacing, open bites, thumb‑sucking habits, and other issues that benefit from an early approach. When indicated, early treatment simplifies later care and can protect front teeth from injury.

image.alt: Young patient receiving early orthodontic care

paragraphs.text: It’s never too late to straighten teeth. As long as gums and bone are healthy, adults can benefit from orthodontic treatment to improve alignment, function, and confidence.

We offer discreet options such as Invisalign<sup>®</sup> (first mention uses ®), Spark™, and Damon Clear ceramic braces. Mild to moderate adult cases often finish in 12 to 18 months with aligners; more complex cases may require fixed appliances or combined approaches.

image.alt: Adult patient smiling during orthodontic treatment

paragraphs.text: Metal brackets bonded to teeth are connected with archwires; periodic adjustments move teeth into position. Metal braces are durable and a dependable option for many cases.

image.alt: Close-up of metal braces on teeth

paragraphs.text: Ceramic (tooth-colored) braces blend with enamel for a less noticeable look. Self-ligating systems such as Damon use a slide mechanism instead of elastic ties to reduce friction and can shorten treatment in many cases.

image.alt: Patient smiling with ceramic braces

paragraphs.text: Bonding appointment, short period of sensitivity, and regular adjustment visits every 6 to 10 weeks. Typical timelines range from under 12 months for minor cases to 18–36 months for more complex treatment, followed by a retention phase.

image.alt: Braces appointment and adjustment

paragraphs.text: You’ll need to modify diet, brush carefully around brackets, and maintain routine visits. After braces come off, retainers help preserve your results.

image.alt: Cleaning teeth while in braces
Two patients with braces smiling

paragraphs.text: Clear aligners are a series of custom trays worn about 20 to 22 hours per day, with each tray worn for one to two weeks to move teeth gradually. Digital 3D scans replace traditional impressions and guide predictable staging.
Aligners suit many mild to moderate spacing and crowding cases and are popular with adults who want a nearly invisible option. Final candidacy is determined during consultation.

image.alt: Clear aligner tray on a model of teeth

paragraphs.text: Jaw surgery is considered when severe skeletal discrepancies cannot be corrected with braces or aligners alone. These cases often involve significant overbite, underbite, or facial asymmetry.

Treatment is coordinated with an oral and maxillofacial surgeon: pre-surgical orthodontics to align teeth, the surgical procedure, then post-surgical orthodontics to fine-tune bite and occlusion. We discuss timeline and expectations at consultation.

image.alt: Orthodontic team consulting on surgical case

paragraphs.text: Retainers preserve your new alignment. Options include removable Essix-style retainers, Hawley retainers with acrylic and wire, and fixed bonded retainers on the lingual side.

Wear retainers full-time immediately after treatment, then taper to nightly wear as directed. Many patients are advised to wear a retainer several nights per week indefinitely. Clean removable retainers daily, avoid heat, and replace warped or broken retainers promptly.

image.alt: Orthodontic retainer shown on a model

paragraphs.text: We use digital X-rays, 3D scanning, and advanced treatment‑planning software to improve diagnostic precision and patient comfort. Digital tools make impressions easier and treatment simulations more predictable.
These technologies often reduce in‑office time, strengthen communication about expected outcomes, and help us deliver efficient, patient-centered care.
Intraoral scanners capture accurate, comfortable digital impressions for aligners and appliances without traditional putty impressions.

image.alt: Intraoral scanner capturing digital impressions

paragraphs.text: High-resolution digital radiography provides detailed images with less radiation than traditional film, aiding accurate diagnosis and treatment planning.

image.alt: Digital X-ray equipment in orthodontic office

paragraphs.text: Software that models staged tooth movements gives you a virtual preview of treatment and helps our team plan efficient, predictable steps.

image.alt: 3D treatment planning software on a computer
Orthodontic office showing digital technology

paragraphs.text: Find clear, practical answers to common questions about treatments, scheduling, insurance, and how to care for braces, aligners, and retainers at Damon Orthodontics.

accordion.header: Which treatment is right for me?

paragraphs.text: The best option depends on your orthodontic needs and goals. Damon Orthodontics offers the Damon System braces (including Damon Clear) and clear aligners such as Invisalign<sup>®</sup> and Spark. Complex cases often need braces; mild-to-moderate concerns can frequently be treated with clear aligners. Schedule a consultation so the doctors can evaluate your smile and recommend the ideal approach.

image.alt: Happy Family Portrait

accordion.header: How long does each treatment take?

paragraphs.text: Treatment time varies by case and method. Clear aligner treatment often takes 12–18 months for mild-to-moderate cases, while traditional braces commonly require 18–36 months depending on complexity. Damon System treatments can sometimes reduce overall time compared with older bracket systems. Your personalized timeline will be provided at the initial visit.

image.alt: Collaborative Team Spirit Moment

paragraphs.text: Some initial soreness or tenderness is normal after placement or adjustments. Modern systems like Damon typically produce less discomfort than older braces; clear aligners usually cause milder pressure-related soreness. Manage discomfort with over-the-counter pain relievers, orthodontic wax for irritated cheeks, cold compresses, saltwater rinses, and a soft diet for a day or two after changes.

image.alt: Couple Enjoying Time Together

accordion.header: What should I do if an aligner is lost or a bracket breaks?

paragraphs.text: Contact the office right away. For a lost aligner you may be asked to wear the previous tray or move to the next set depending on your treatment stage. For broken brackets or wires, protect soft tissues with orthodontic wax and call to schedule a repair. We will give specific instructions based on the issue and urgency.

image.alt: Smiling Man Working at Desk

accordion.header: Will my insurance cover treatment and what payment options are available?

paragraphs.text: Many dental insurance plans provide some orthodontic benefits. Damon Orthodontics works with most major carriers and can accept direct carrier payments. We offer interest-free monthly payment plans and family discounts to make treatment manageable. For a full estimate bring insurance information to your complimentary consultation.

image.alt: Mother and Daughter Smiling Together

accordion.header: How and when can I schedule an appointment?

paragraphs.text: You do not need a referral — patients may schedule directly. Routine adjustment frequency depends on treatment type: Damon System patients often return every 6–10 weeks, traditional braces may require more frequent visits, and aligner check-ins follow your individualized plan. Use our online request page or call the office to find a convenient time.

image.alt: Happy Family Portrait

accordion.header: How do I care for braces, aligners, and retainers?

paragraphs.text: Braces: avoid hard, crunchy, and sticky foods; brush carefully around brackets and use interdental brushes or floss threaders as needed. Aligners: remove for eating, clean trays daily, and wear them about 20–22 hours per day. Retainers: rinse after meals, brush gently, keep them in a protective case, and replace lost or damaged retainers promptly. Proper care helps treatment progress and protects your investment.

image.alt: Couple Enjoying Time Together

accordion.header: Can adults get orthodontic treatment or start treatment during pregnancy?

paragraphs.text: Yes, adults commonly receive orthodontic care with braces or clear aligners. Beginning or continuing treatment during pregnancy is possible; discuss your plan with your orthodontist and your obstetric provider so we can coordinate care safely and comfortably.
